title: Adaptive-runtime evidence-integrity closeout verification
scope: Verify the narrow correctness-only evidence-integrity closeout for catalog outcome derivation, exact release and classification correlation, composite accounting, and complete immutable projection validation without changing runtime mechanisms or releasing measurement.

All v1 and v2 documents retain their original semantics.
Measurement, interaction execution, campaigns, transforms, CI, push, active_internal, and production activation remain unauthorized.
procedure: Validate every additive schema and canonical catalog.
Prove outcome derivation and retention change from catalog-only changes and reject zero or multiple matches.

Resolve exact classification targets and exhaustively enforce the canonical compatibility matrix.

Validate all fifteen immutable projection inputs, hashes, and required joins.
Reject self-hashed but semantically unrelated host, binary, workload, metric, classification, and materialization inputs.
Rebuild the supplied materializations and projection twice and compare canonical bytes and hashes.
Re-run foundation, compiler/manifest, runtime-evidence, and hardening regressions.
Run focused builds, requirement-home tests, SpecTrace validation, and git diff --check.
expected_result: Catalog-owned outcomes, authoritative release ordering, exact classification identity, closed compatibility, composite operation accounting, and a complete fifteen-input recomputing projection validate deterministically while prior contracts remain valid and measurement and activation remain frozen.
status_summary: Passed on 2026-07-25 after six additive schemas, fifteen immutable inputs, nine catalog mappings, nine invalid evidence cases, eight invalid classification cases, all 66 classification pairs, seven invalid projection substitutions, prior checkpoint regressions, both focused Release builds, four requirement homes, direct SpecTrace model validation, deterministic rebuilds, and diff validation completed without runtime mechanism change, another-axis migration, interaction execution, performance work, CI change, push, active_internal, or production activation.
